subject: physiology
title: Platelet Adhesion, Activation, and Primary Haemostasis

steps.tx: The arrest of bleeding following vascular endothelial disruption relies upon an orchestrated sequence designated haemostasis. Primary haemostasis culminates in the rapid formation of a temporary platelet plug, initiated within seconds of injury by **platelet adhesion**, where circulating anucleate disc-shaped platelets adhere firmly to exposed subendothelial extracellular matrix proteins.
steps.say: Primary haemostasis arrests bleeding through a platelet plug. Within seconds of endothelial injury, platelets adhere to exposed subendothelial collagen.

nodes.label: Von Willebrand Factor Binds Exposed Fibrillar Collagen
Platelet Glycoprotein Ib/IX Complexes Tether to Bound vWF
Platelet Shape Change and Release of Granule Mediators

steps.tx: Under conditions of high hydrodynamic shear stress within arteriolar microvessels, platelet adhesion requires the multimeric plasma glycoprotein **von Willebrand factor**. Synthesized by endothelial Weibel-Palade bodies and megakaryocytes, vWF uncoils in high shear to bind exposed collagen, presenting A1 domains that tether platelet glycoprotein Ib/IX/V receptor complexes to arrest rolling platelets.
steps.say: Under high shear stress, multimeric von Willebrand factor binds collagen and tethers platelet glycoprotein Ib/IX complexes to arrest rolling platelets.

vis.alt: Endothelial von Willebrand factor secretion and platelet tethering.
vis.caption: High-shear platelet adhesion mediated by multimeric von Willebrand factor. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Genetic defects in this initial tethering mechanism produce severe bleeding diatheses. In **Bernard-Soulier syndrome**, congenital deficiency of the platelet glycoprotein Ib/IX/V receptor complex prevents platelet adhesion to vWF, presenting with severe mucosal bleeding, giant platelets on peripheral smear, and isolated thrombocytopenia that fails to agglutinate with ristocetin.
steps.say: Bernard-Soulier syndrome is caused by GP Ib/IX deficiency, preventing vWF binding and causing mucosal bleeding with giant platelets.

vis.alt: Platelet glycoprotein Ib receptor deficiency in Bernard Soulier syndrome.
vis.caption: Defective platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor in Bernard-Soulier syndrome. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Adhesion triggers profound intracellular signaling, converting smooth discoid platelets into spiky spheres with extended pseudopodia. Calcium surges activate phospholipase A2, liberating membrane arachidonic acid, which cyclooxygenase-1 and thromboxane synthase convert into **thromboxane A2**. Thromboxane A2 serves as a potent autocrine and paracrine agonist, inducing intense localized vasoconstriction and activating neighboring platelets.
steps.say: Adhesion stimulates cyclooxygenase-1 to produce thromboxane A2, a potent agonist that causes vasoconstriction and recruits adjacent platelets.

left.title: Platelet Thromboxane A2
points: Promotes platelet activation and dense granule release
Irreversibly blocked by low-dose aspirin (75-100 mg)

right.title: Endothelial Prostacyclin (PGI2)
points: Synthesized by intact endothelial COX-1 and COX-2
Elevates intracellular cyclic AMP in platelets
Potent inhibitor of platelet activation and aggregation
Promotes local vasodilation to limit thrombus size

steps.tx: Concurrently, activated platelets undergo exocytic degranulation. Dense delta-granules discharge adenosine diphosphate, calcium, and serotonin, while alpha-granules release fibrinogen, fibronectin, platelet factor 4, and platelet-derived growth factor. Extracellular **adenosine diphosphate** binds platelet P2Y1 and P2Y12 purinergic receptors, stimulating adenylyl cyclase inhibition and sustained calcium mobilization.
steps.say: Platelets degranulate ADP and serotonin from dense granules, and fibrinogen from alpha granules. ADP binds P2Y12 receptors to amplify platelet activation.

steps.tx: The culminating event in primary haemostasis is **platelet aggregation**, mediated by inside-out conformational activation of the integrin alpha-IIb-beta-3 (glycoprotein IIb/IIIa) receptor complex. Activated glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors bind multivalent dimeric plasma fibrinogen molecules, which cross-link adjacent platelets into an expanding primary haemostatic plug.
steps.say: Aggregation occurs when activated glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors bind circulating fibrinogen, cross-linking neighboring platelets into a primary plug.

steps.tx: Congenital failure of platelet aggregation occurs in **Glanzmann thrombasthenia**, an autosomal recessive bleeding disorder caused by deficiency or dysfunction of glycoprotein IIb/IIIa. Platelet count and morphology are normal, and platelet adhesion to subendothelium remains intact, but platelets fail to aggregate in response to ADP, collagen, or thrombin, causing lifelong mucocutaneous haemorrhage.
steps.say: Glanzmann thrombasthenia is caused by glycoprotein IIb/IIIa deficiency, impairing aggregation and causing severe mucocutaneous bleeding despite normal platelet count.

left.title: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome
points: Deficiency of GP Ib/IX/V receptor complex
Impaired platelet adhesion to subendothelial vWF
Fails to agglutinate with ristocetin; normal with ADP

right.title: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia
points: Deficiency of GP IIb/IIIa integrin complex
Normal platelet count and normal platelet size
Normal agglutination with ristocetin; fails with ADP and thrombin

steps.tx: Primary haemostatic plug stability remains fragile until consolidated by secondary haemostasis. Activated platelets expose negatively charged **phosphatidylserine** on their outer membrane leaflet, creating a catalytic phospholipid scaffold. This procoagulant surface binds clotting factor complexes, accelerating thrombin generation thousand-fold to transform soluble fibrinogen into a rigid, permanent cross-linked fibrin meshwork.
steps.say: Activated platelets flip phosphatidylserine to their outer surface, providing a catalytic membrane scaffold that accelerates clotting factors to generate fibrin.
